- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) in last 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment unit.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 75% of forecast’s 1st/2nd day, assume model is overconfident; apply 10–15% downward correction for first 5 days.
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in last 5 days correlates with forecast divergence; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×forecast + 0.3×prior true) to dampen noise.
